research_concepts: causal effect of prior action on play outcome
measurement reliability of derived play types
methodological_questions: lookahead bias in identifying drive before PNR
possession boundary definition and correct ordering
confounding by game state and defensive quality
label reliability (DRIVE, PNR) and bias from foul leakage
exposure sparsity (how often does a teammate drive precede a PNR?)
regression to the mean in PNR PPP
mechanical floor effects from foul-ending possessions

historical_evidence.finding: Defensive scheme change detection with inferred labels produced near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise, making the question untestable.
Play-type label backfill verification failed: PNR 28.7% FAIL (outside 20-28% band), 3100 games with team PNR >33%, PULL_UP near 0-1% for many teams, and team identity FAIL. Labels are not reliable.
Labeling on-ball defensive coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) had confident label rates of only 14.9% and 3.3%, with switches_on unpopulated; unanswerable with the data.

OTHER possessions had 36% foul endings, inflating PPP; DRIVE PPP was 12pp below foul benchmark (foul leakage); only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type. PPP differences are labeling artifacts, not real efficiency.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme changes from play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Inferred labels cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilling and verifying play-type label distributions
failed_approaches.why: Distributional failures (team PNR >33%, PULL_UP ~0-1%) and team-identity mismatch, indicating pervasive label misclassification.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverages from matchup/PBP data
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates too low (3-15%) and critical fields unpopulated; question unanswerable with available data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type PPP to measure real offensive efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Systematic foul leakage: OTHER possessions artificially inflated by foul endings, DRIVE PPP depressed; only 0.7% map to real play type via initiation_type.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels, including DRIVE and PNR, are highly unreliable and affected by systematic misclassification and foul leakage artifacts.
PPP differences across play types cannot be taken as genuine efficiency differences without thorough label validation.
Label coverage and confidence are very low for some actions, making sequence identification difficult.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate drive preceding a PNR causally raises PNR PPP.
The magnitude or sign of any correlation between a prior drive and PNR efficiency, even in the defective labels.
Whether the possession-graph derived play-type records have been improved since the audited data.
The prevalence of the teammate-drive-before-PNR sequence in the 2022-2026 data.
own_inferences: Given the documented DRIVE foul leakage (depressed PPP) and PNR label failures (distributional anomalies), any test of the sequential hypothesis would likely pick up labeling artifacts rather than genuine effects.
Even if the sequence is common, misclassification of either the drive or the PNR action would dilute or bias the estimated conditional PPP.
The possession graph's derivation from play-by-play cannot escape the underlying label quality issues unless a completely re-validated labeling system is built.
uncertainties: Whether the graph database's 'derived play-type possession records' incorporate any post-audit label corrections not captured in the retrieved families.
The season scope of the label audits; they may have been run on 2023-24 or 2024-25 data, and 2025-26 labels might be different, though no evidence indicates improvement.
The exact definition of 'any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR' and how it would be operationalized from the possession graph.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the historical evidence, one might have assumed the play-type labels were reliable enough for a sequential analysis. The retrieved families show pervasive misclassification, foul leakage, and label failures that render the required DRIVE and PNR labels untrustworthy. This directly undermines testability and changed the decision from potentially proceeding to do_not_proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: DRIVE and PNR labels exhibit distributional failures, foul leakage, and low mapping rates; misclassification would bias any comparison of PNR PPP conditional on a prior drive.
The independent variable (a teammate drive occurring before the PNR) cannot be reliably measured, and the outcome (PNR PPP) may itself be mislabeled.

prior_work.summary: No prior study directly tested the sequential effect of a teammate drive on PNR PPP. However, multiple studies have shown that the play-type labels essential for the question are severely compromised by misclassification and foul artifacts, effectively precluding a valid test without major label improvements.

risks.text: DRIVE label foul leakage (12pp below benchmark) and PNR label distribution failures risk spurious or masked relationships.
Both the exposure (teammate drive before PNR) and the outcome (PNR PPP) rely on labels that fail validation checks.
Game state (score margin, shot clock, period), defensive quality, and possession origin could confound the relationship, and any residual confounding would compound with label error.
It is unknown how often a possession contains both a teammate drive and a later PNR; if the sequence is rare, statistical power will be extremely low.
Foul-ending possessions are misclassified in DRIVE labels, which could create a mechanical floor/ceiling effect that biases PPP comparisons.

design.estimand: Average treatment effect of having at least one teammate drive occur in the same possession before the pick-and-roll action on the points scored on that pick-and-roll possession, among possessions that contain a clear terminal PNR.
design.unit: NBA possession, defined as a continuous offensive stint ending in a made/missed field goal, free throws, or turnover.
design.sample: All possessions from NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs where a pick-and-roll play type is identified as the terminal action, excluding possessions with ambiguous action sequences or conflicting labels.
design.power: Unknown; requires a preliminary count of eligible sequences. The effect size needed for 80% power at α=0.05 would be estimated via simulation after label-quality filters are applied.
design.controls: Possession start type (after made basket, after miss, after turnover, after dead ball), game score margin, period, seconds remaining, offensive team identity, defensive team identity, and a control for defensive scheme (if available and reliable).
design.falsification: 1) Test whether a drive that occurs *after* the PNR in the same possession is associated with a different PNR PPP (should be null or explainable by reverse causality). 2) Restrict analysis to team-games where PNR share falls within an acceptable historical band (e.g., 20–28%) and DRIVE foul leakage is within ±3 percentage points of a validated benchmark. Result should be consistent.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered hypothesis; if multiple temporal windows for the drive are tested, use Holm-Bonferroni correction.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if (a) a new label validation study demonstrates that DRIVE and PNR labels in the target seasons meet pre-specified accuracy and completeness thresholds, and (b) the eligible sample yields at least 5000 qualifying possessions. Use a permutation test with possession-level randomization to compare PNR PPP, with a two-sided α=0.05.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play and derived possession graph as of 2026-06-14, commit snapshotted for reproducibility.

args.query: Does a teammate drive before a pick-and-roll increase the pick-and-roll's points per possession?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
We need to identify research concepts and methodological questions for the retrieval.

Research question: "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP." This is about play-type labeling: a "DRIVE" (an action type) by a teammate, occurring before a pick-and-roll (PNR) by the same team, and its effect on the points per possession (PPP) of that PNR. So we're looking at sequences: a DRIVE by a teammate, then a PNR (presumably by another player or even the same? "teammate DRIVE" implies a different player than the PNR initiator? Actually "teammate DRIVE" means a drive by any teammate of the PNR ball-handler? The question is ambiguous. But the core concepts: possessional sequencing, play-type labeling, DRIVE action, PNR action, PPP outcome. Methodological questions: how to define possession sequence? How to ensure causality? Potential confounders (defense, game situation, player fatigue). The question is about raising PNR PPP, so it's a causal effect of a preceding drive. So we need to retrieve historical evidence on similar sequencing studies, issues with play-type labeling, reliability of drive and PNR labels, sequence-based analysis, potential lookahead bias, mechanical floor effects, etc.

We need to craft a query and list research_concepts and methodological_questions.

Research concepts: play-type labeling, pick-and-roll, drive, possession sequencing, points per possession, NBA tracking data, causal inference in basketball sequences.

Methodological questions: lookahead bias in sequence labeling, reliability of derived play-type labels, possession boundary definition, confounding by game state, sample size for specific sequence patterns, regression to the mean, selection bias from non-random possession starts, labeling errors in action types (DRIVE vs. other), outcome measurement (PPP definition), mechanical floor effects (e.g., PNR may end with a shot or turnover; preceding drive might affect defensive positioning), and generalizability across seasons.

We'll query: "Does a teammate drive before a pick-and-roll increase the pick-and-roll's points per possession?" with research concepts and methodological questions.

Let's call retrieve_history with appropriate args.

We are in stage 2, after retrieval. We have four records: FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-CHT-025. We need to populate the output schema.

First, let's understand the research question: "Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP." It asks whether a possession that includes a teammate drive (by someone other than the PNR initiator? Or any teammate drive?) before a pick-and-roll leads to higher points per possession for that PNR. So it's about sequence: a drive occurs first, then a pick-and-roll action later in the same possession, and we compare PPP for PNRs that had a prior teammate drive vs. those that did not.

Need to identify concepts: play-type labeling (DRIVE, PNR), possession sequencing, PPP, causal inference about sequence effects.

Methodological questions: lookahead bias (if drive and PNR are identified using information from after the PNR, or if possession end result biases labeling), possession boundary definition (how are possessions segmented? Is a drive and a PNR in same possession correctly identified?), confounding by game state (maybe drives precede PNRs when defense is already broken, leading to higher PPP not caused by the drive), labeling reliability (are DRIVE and PNR labels accurate? evidence suggests no), sample size, regression to the mean, mechanical floor effects.

Now, extract historical evidence from the four records.

Record FAM:SF-APPA-005: Defensive scheme change. Not directly about our question, but about inferred labels and label error. Status: untestable. Finding: within-game change 61.0%, cross-game 67.7%, near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise. It has risk LABEL_ERROR. This is relevant because it shows that labeling (even defensive schemes) is noisy, which could affect our ability to reliably label drives and PNRs.

Record FAM:SF-APPA-030: Play-type label backfill verification. Status: inconclusive. Finding: PNR 28.7% FAIL, PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL, PNR PPP 0.948 PASS, temporal PASS, team identity FAIL, 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams. Final: FAIL. It has risk LABEL_ERROR, limitation label_or_classification_error. This directly impacts our ability to use play-type labels for DRIVE and PNR. The labels are unreliable.

Record FAM:SF-APPS-058: Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels. Status: untestable. Finding: low confident label rates (14.9% and 3.3%), switches_on unpopulated. Failure: unanswerable, label error, small sample. Also relevant: labeling of defensive actions is poor.

Record FAM:SF-CHT-025: Play-type labeling audit: OTHER/DRIVE foul leakage. Status: artifact. Finding: OTHER 36% end in fouls, PPP inflated; DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark; PNR shows 22% foul rate; only 0.7% map to a real play type via initiation_type. This is crucial: DRIVE label has major foul leakage issues, potentially misclassifying possessions, and the overall mapping of play types is problematic. So using DRIVE labels would be suspect.

Now, we need to populate historical_evidence list with these records, using id and status_as_recorded exactly. status_as_recorded: "untestable" for FAM:SF-APPA-005 and FAM:SF-APPS-058, "inconclusive" for FAM:SF-APPA-030, "artifact" for FAM:SF-CHT-025. They are as written.

failed_approaches: identify the approaches that failed. FAM:SF-APPA-005: using inferred defensive labels for scheme change failed due to label noise. FAM:SF-APPA-030: backfilling play-type labels resulted in failures due to labeling errors. FAM:SF-APPS-058: labeling on-ball coverage from NBA matchup/PBP fields unanswerable due to low label rate. FAM:SF-CHT-025: examining PPP differences as real efficiency failed due to foul artifacts in labeling. So we can list them.

evidence_establishes: what the records tell us. They establish that play-type labels (including DRIVE and PNR) from the available data sources are unreliable, with significant misclassification, foul leakage, and low coverage, and that using these labels for causal inference is risky. They do not directly test the specific sequential effect of a teammate drive on PNR PPP. But they heavily undermine the feasibility.

evidence_does_not_establish: whether a teammate drive preceding a PNR has any causal effect; whether even with perfect labels the question could be answered; potential confounders; sample size; any actual test of the question.

own_inferences: based on the evidence, it's likely that the DRIVE and PNR labels are too noisy and biased (foul leakage) to test this question reliably. The possession sequencing might also be problematic (need to correctly order actions within a possession). So testability is low.

uncertainties: exact nature of the graph database's "derived play-type possession records" might be different from the labels audited, but given the records indicate widespread labeling issues, it's uncertain whether improvements have been made. Also, the 2025-26 data may have different labeling quality, but nothing suggests it.

historical_effect: changed_decision? The historical evidence makes me think the question is likely untestable due to label reliability. I might decide do_not_proceed.

testability: p_testable low, e.g., 0.1 or 0.2. Blocking constraints: LABEL_ERROR, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, possibly others.

prior_work: already_answered: partly? No, no prior work directly tested the sequential effect. But related work on labeling failures. So "partly" might be appropriate, citing FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025, etc.

risks: LABEL_ERROR, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, also CONFOUNDING (game state, defense quality), BASE_RATE (maybe drives preceding PNRs are rare, leading to exposure sparsity), SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL (PNR PPP might be affected by labeling of PNR). Also, the foul leakage in DRIVE label is concerning for mechanical floor effects? MECHANICAL_FLOOR: if a possession ends with a foul, it might be classified differently, but here DRIVE label leaks fouls that should be OTHER, so DRIVE PPP is depressed, PNR PPP might be inflated? Need to think. Actually, the foul leakage could create spurious relationships: if a possession contains a PNR and ends in a foul, the PNR might be mislabeled or the PPP higher due to fouls? FAM:SF-CHT-025 says PNR shows 22% foul rate, but not necessarily leakage. However, the DRIVE foul leakage means that DRIVE possessions that end in fouls are being labeled as OTHER, so the remaining DRIVE possessions have lower PPP. If we condition on a DRIVE preceding a PNR, the DRIVE label might be missing when fouls occur, which could bias the sample. So that's a confound.

predicted_outcome: I'd assign high probability to "artifact" or "untestable" because of labeling issues. So supported low, rejected low, untestable high, artifact moderate, uncertain moderate. Let's say untestable 0.5, artifact 0.3, uncertain 0.2.

decision: do_not_proceed.

design: still required. Even if do_not_proceed, outline the minimal viable test. So I'll describe a design but note that label reliability must be addressed first.

Now, construct the JSON. Ensure all required fields are present.

I'll also use the glossary and data_catalog tools? I could, to better understand the data, but I should not assume facts not seen. The task statement already describes the data available. I can check data_catalog() to see what fields might be relevant for possession sequencing, but it's not strictly necessary. The retrieval results already indicate labeling issues. But to be thorough, I might call glossary() for definitions of "possession" and "play type" terms? I have tool calls remaining (budget 12). I could make additional calls to get more details on the study families? Maybe read_family on one of them to get more detail, but not required. I think I have enough to make the assessment. However, I'll call glossary and data_catalog to ensure I don't miss anything. But the schema asks for design fields like "unit", "sample", etc. I need to construct a design even if do_not_proceed. So I'll outline a plan: estimand: difference in PNR PPP between possessions where a teammate drive occurred in the same possession before the PNR vs. not. Unit: possession. Sample: NBA 2022-2026 regular/playoffs from play-by-play derived possession graph. But I'll note that label quality is a blocker.

But before final, I need to output the JSON. I'll craft it.

I'll include historical_evidence with all four records. For each, status_as_recorded: I'll copy exactly: for FAM:SF-APPA-005: "untestable"; FAM:SF-APPA-030: "inconclusive"; FAM:SF-APPS-058: "untestable"; FAM:SF-CHT-025: "artifact". The finding text: I'll summarize the observed_result and relevant context.

failed_approaches: For each record, what_failed and why. For example, for FAM:SF-CHT-025, what_failed: "Using play-type PPP differences to assess real efficiency" and why: "Foul leakage misclassifies possessions, inflating OTHER PPP and depressing DRIVE PPP." For FAM:SF-APPA-005, what_failed: "Inferring defensive scheme changes from play-type labels", why: "Label noise makes transition matrices near-uniform, indistinguishable from random." For FAM:SF-APPA-030, what_failed: "Backfilling play-type labels to verify distributional consistency", why: "Distributional failures (team PNR >33%, PULL_UP near 0%) and label errors." For FAM:SF-APPS-058, what_failed: "Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup/PBP fields", why: "Low confident label rate (3-15%) and missing data (switches_on)."

evidence_does_not_establish: etc.

It's uncertain if the 2025-26 data has the same issues.

risks: list a few: LABEL_ERROR, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, CONFOUNDING, BASE_RATE (maybe), MECHANICAL_FLOOR? Possibly the fouling issue creates mechanical floor effect. I'll include RISK:LABEL_ERROR, RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RISK:CONFOUNDING (e.g., game state, defensive quality, shot clock), RISK:OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL (PNR PPP is derived from possession outcomes and play labels, so mislabeling affects both exposure and outcome). I could also include RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR because fouls that end possessions may be systematically misclassified, leading to biased PPP. But I'll stick to the most prominent.

predicted_outcome: probabilities summing to 1. I'll assign: supported 0.05, rejected 0.05, untestable 0.5, artifact 0.3, uncertain 0.1. Check sum: 1.0.

decision: "do_not_proceed".

design: even so, I'll provide a minimal viable design. Estimand: average treatment effect of a teammate drive occurring in the same possession before the PNR on the points scored on that PNR possession, conditional on the PNR being the terminal play type. Unit: NBA possession ending in a PNR (with a clear PNR action). Sample: all seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 with available play-by-play, after excluding possessions with ambiguous action sequences or missing labels. Multiplicity: single hypothesis test; adjust if multiple sequence windows tested. Decision rule: pre-register threshold for label quality (e.g., exclude team-games with PNR share >33% or DRIVE foul leakage >X) and a minimum sample size; use permutation test of possession-level PPP difference. Data version: commit date of play-by-play and derived possession graph as of 2026-06-14. However, due to documented label errors, the design would require a preliminary study to validate label accuracy, which is not yet achieved. So I'll note that.

Now, I'll output the final JSON.
